import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


sns.set(style='whitegrid', context='talk')


latino_df = df_combined[df_combined['Race and Ethnicity'] == 'Hispanic or Latino']


major_counts = latino_df.groupby('Major')['Awards/Degrees Conferred'].sum().reset_index()


major_counts = major_counts.sort_values('Awards/Degrees Conferred', ascending=False)


major_counts['Major Short'] = major_counts['Major'].str.replace(r'^\d{2}\.\d{2,4} - ', '', regex=True)



plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
barplot = sns.barplot(
    data=major_counts,
    y='Major Short',
    x='Awards/Degrees Conferred',
    palette='crest'
)


plt.title('Top 20 Majors by Number of Latino Doctorate Graduates (2021–2023)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Number of Graduates')
plt.ylabel('Major')
plt.tight_layout()


for index, row in major_counts.iterrows():
    barplot.text(row['Awards/Degrees Conferred'], index, row['Awards/Degrees Conferred'], color='black', va="center")

plt.show()

title: Welcome to the Majors Page
text:
Welcome to the Majors Page
Welcome to our website. This platform is designed to support faculty hiring committees by providing clear, accessible insights into the landscape of earned doctorates. Here, you’ll find data and visualizations that highlight trends in doctoral degrees across disciplines, with a focus on promoting equity and informed decision-making in the hiring process. Our goal is to equip committees with the tools and context necessary to understand who is earning doctorates and how that knowledge can inform inclusive and forward-thinking faculty recruitment.
